rows: A macaque has three kinds of cone, most sensitive near 430, 531 and 561 nanometres. That is close to your own three, so colours look much as they do to you.

A rhesus monkey reaches about 26 cycles per degree by seven weeks of age, close to a person's 30. A marmoset's cone mosaic could carry about 30 near the fovea. A grey mouse lemur manages only about 4 to 5.

Owl monkeys have a single cone type, lack colour vision and are active at night. Male marmosets have two cone types. Howler monkeys are fully trichromatic. This view shows the three-cone pattern of macaques.
Macaques, squirrel monkeys and marmosets have a clear fovea, a small pit where vision is sharpest. Owl monkeys have only a rudimentary one. We draw no separate sharp centre.
Neurons in macaque visual cortex respond to the small difference between the two eyes' images, which supports stereoscopic depth. A phone has one camera, so this view leaves that cue out.
The single sharpness of 26 is the app's pick from a wide spread of measured values. The colour matrix is the app's mapping from three pigment peaks. The colour drawing is the app's own.

claims.how: The value equals the 26.3 cycles per degree that rhesus monkeys reached, which was the highest level the test assessed.
The matrix name stands for a matrix built from the peaks 430, 531 and 561 nm that R31 gives for a cynomolgus monkey, with R32 giving 530 nm and R23 giving 561 nm.
The peaks 430, 531 and 561 nm come from R31, and each lies within 2 nm of a cited peak (430 R31, 530 R32, 561 R23).

quotes.quote: achieving the maximum acuity level assessed (26.3 c/deg) by 7 weeks of age for most monkeys
The wave-lengths of maximum sensitivity were approximately 430, 531 and 561 nm, respectively.
L and M genes encoding pigments with λmax values of 530 and 558 nm, respectively
we determined exact peak absorption spectrum (λmax) of all three allelic pigments, red, yellow, and green, of the marmoset, to be 561, 553, and 539nm, respectively
